title: Amazon snaps up Decart’s AI optimization tech for $7.5B as it prepares to sell Trainium chips
lede: Amazon is paying a reported $7.5 billion for Decart's optimization technology plus its founders and research team, as it gets ready to sell Trainium chips to outside customers.

points: Bloomberg reported the price; Amazon described the deal in a blog post.
Decart, an Israeli startup, is known for real-time interactive world models, most recently Oasis 3, and for AI video generation tools.
Its Decart Optimization Stack (DOS) helps models run efficiently on Nvidia, Amazon and Google hardware.
Amazon gets the DOS technology, the founding team and Decart's AI researchers and engineers, not the whole company.
Amazon has so far run Trainium only in its own data centers and now plans to sell the chips as an alternative to Nvidia.

sections.text: Software that makes models run well on non-Nvidia silicon is what makes moving a workload to Trainium practical. With DOS in house, Amazon aims to lower the cost of switching for teams tuned to Nvidia.
